title: Control Plane Evidence Graph
assertions: every evidence chain must connect observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next loop
change and verifier refs must point to existing repository files or package directories
artifact evidence refs are names only and must stay redacted
evidence graph records explain why a loop exists without relying on narrative memory
frontend handoff decisions that change thread semantics must connect to the closed-loop claim that enforces them
cross-repository lifecycle observations must become owned open questions when this repository cannot safely change the runtime owner
evidence graph evidence must publish generated_at and expires_at and refresh on a schedule

chains.observation: Provider and smoke harness failures could previously end as isolated artifacts.
chains.hypothesis: Redacted harness summaries can be transformed into closed-loop candidate records.
chains.decision: Harness failures are promoted into closed-loop candidate artifacts that require claim binding, verifier, CI gate, redacted evidence, decision record, and evidence graph edge before adoption.

chains.observation: Redacted live workflow summaries could be reused after their evidence window expired, allowing stale harness output to create fresh closed-loop candidates.
chains.hypothesis: Stamping generated_at and expires_at in the redacted summary, then rejecting expired summaries in harness promotion, prevents stale observations from entering the closed-loop backlog.
chains.decision: Harness promotion now treats evidence freshness as a merge gate: expired or malformed summary freshness metadata cannot produce closed-loop candidate evidence.

chains.observation: The AI Agent load harness produced useful stress evidence, but failures could remain a standalone load artifact instead of becoming a closed-loop adoption candidate.
chains.hypothesis: Scheduling the load harness and routing its redacted live summary through harness promotion lets performance or reliability failures enter the same candidate intake path as smoke failures.
chains.decision: Load/stress failures now have the same closed-loop promotion path as smoke failures: daily evidence refresh, redacted summary, candidate artifact, intake, and decision records.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidates named required artifact types, but the candidate artifact did not itself carry executable commands for producing or verifying those artifacts.
chains.hypothesis: Embedding an adoption_plan in each candidate lets agents act from the artifact even if they do not read the surrounding documentation.
chains.decision: Candidate artifacts now carry an adoption_plan, and both intake and decision verification reject candidates whose plan does not cover every required next artifact.

chains.observation: Business claims could change without bound code or tests changing in the same pull request.
chains.hypothesis: Comparing the PR diff against the loop registry can force claim meaning changes to co-change bound code or test paths, not just manifests or generated docs.
chains.decision: PR impact verification rejects claim meaning changes when the diff only changes manifests or generated docs; at least one bound code or test path must move.

chains.observation: The loop registry could reject semantic drift internally while its evidence artifact did not show each claim's code, test, manifest, generated doc, verifier, and target command surface to downstream agents.
chains.hypothesis: Publishing per-claim surface evidence with target verifier commands lets agents infer the required co-change and QA scope from machine evidence instead of relying on narrative docs or memory.
chains.decision: Claim surface binding and target verifier commands are now visible in loop-registry evidence and generated docs, so AI agents can detect code/test/doc and QA scope from verifier output even when they skip prose.

chains.observation: Claim verifier commands existed in the loop-registry evidence artifact, but a reviewer or agent still had to open artifacts or run jq before seeing the exact target QA command in a PR check.
chains.hypothesis: Emitting GitHub Actions annotations from the same loop-registry evidence surface makes the target verifier commands visible in CI without adding another narrative handoff.
chains.decision: Loop-registry PR checks now surface claim verifier commands as GitHub annotations, keeping QA scope visible even when artifacts and prose are skipped.

chains.observation: Deleting an AI Agent can accidentally remove or hide historical task thread replies if the read model depends on the live agent row.
chains.hypothesis: Capturing an agent snapshot on the thread and falling back to that snapshot for deleted agents keeps prior replies, results, and progress visible.
chains.decision: Deleted-agent thread retention is a closed-loop claim: historical AI thread records use captured agent snapshots instead of disappearing with the mutable agent row.

chains.observation: A user reply inside an AI Agent thread can disappear after refresh if v3 history only projects the latest agent status.
chains.hypothesis: Persisting user follow-up messages as thread history rows and replaying them into v3 history preserves human-agent 티키타카 after reload.
chains.decision: User follow-up retention is enforced as v3 history behavior, not frontend memory.

chains.observation: Two different AI Agents can use the same provider runtime, so provider-based dedupe can collapse independent task assignments and threads.
chains.hypothesis: Assignment and thread identity must stay agent/assignment scoped even when provider/runtime_kind is identical.
chains.decision: Same-provider multi-assignment is a thread identity claim: provider/runtime labels are display metadata, not dedupe keys.

chains.observation: Frontend implementation needed a stable key to distinguish same-agent reassignment from follow-up replies inside an existing AI Agent comment card.
chains.hypothesis: Binding conversation_id and parent_thread_id to the v3 thread history contract, generated frontend handoff, runtime projection tests, and loop-registry claim prevents provider or agent based dedupe from collapsing distinct conversations.
chains.decision: AI Thread History v3 comment card grouping is a closed-loop claim: conversation_id groups the card, parent_thread_id links follow-up runs, and same-agent reassignment receives a distinct conversation.

chains.observation: Loop registry and evidence graph evidence could prove shape but not freshness because the artifacts lacked generated_at and expires_at, and the evidence graph workflow did not run unless code changed.
chains.hypothesis: Self-expiring evidence artifacts plus a scheduled evidence graph workflow let tools detect stale reasoning evidence and refresh it without a human reminder.
chains.decision: Core loop reasoning evidence now carries a 24h freshness window and the evidence graph refreshes daily, so stale loop evidence is machine-detectable.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidate artifacts could be produced without a scheduled intake verifier that reads them, and an intake verifier could report evidence without being tied to the current candidate artifact.
chains.hypothesis: A candidate intake tool can require explicit redacted candidate input and verify producer, loop registry, graph, and adoption artifact requirements.
chains.decision: Candidate intake is scheduled and cannot produce evidence without explicit candidate input, redaction, producer linkage, graph linkage, and adoption artifact requirements.

chains.observation: The loop registry verifier was upgraded to check every expiring loop, but the registry wording could still describe only 24h loops and mislead future agents.
chains.hypothesis: Promoting the refresh-scope rule to a claim and rejecting stale 24h-only wording keeps the SSOT, verifier, and generated reader aligned.
chains.decision: All expiring loops, including long-expiry queues, are now covered by scheduled refresh verification and stale 24h-only SSOT language fails.

chains.observation: A refresh workflow can be edited without carrying the loop id it refreshes, leaving agents to infer semantic ownership from file names or prose.
chains.hypothesis: Requiring RIIDO_LOOP_IDS in every refresh workflow makes loop ownership executable and lets the registry verifier catch workflow-only drift.
chains.decision: Refresh workflows now declare their loop identities directly, so workflow-only edits cannot silently detach scheduled QA from the loop registry.

chains.observation: Loop registry evidence exposed refresh workflow maps and cadence maps, but an agent still had to compose the manual QA refresh command and evidence artifact set itself.
chains.hypothesis: A per-loop refresh_plans evidence surface lets agents and reviewers identify expired-evidence QA commands directly from machine evidence.
chains.decision: Loop registry evidence now exposes refresh_plans with workflow, cadence, expiry, evidence artifacts, and manual refresh commands for every loop.

chains.observation: Candidate intake can verify adoption requirements, but a candidate decision verifier can still be run without the candidate artifact and report decision evidence that is not tied to the current candidate set.
chains.hypothesis: A candidate decision tool can require an explicit candidate artifact, force each redacted candidate to bind owner, priority, disposition, next loop, next artifact, and reject stale decision records that no longer map to a current candidate.
chains.decision: Candidate decisions are scheduled and cannot verify without candidate input, omit owner, priority, disposition, next loop, or next artifact, or retain orphan decisions after the candidate artifact changes.

chains.observation: Closed-loop candidate decisions could name an arbitrary next_artifact even when the consumed candidate artifact declared a bounded adoption artifact set.
chains.hypothesis: Comparing each decision next_artifact against the candidate required_next_artifacts keeps harness failures on an executable adoption path.
chains.decision: Candidate decisions now prove that the selected next artifact is one of the candidate's required executable adoption artifacts.

chains.observation: Candidate decision evidence selected a next_artifact but did not expose the executable command from the consumed candidate adoption_plan.
chains.hypothesis: Copying the selected adoption command into decision evidence lets agents continue from the decision artifact without reopening narrative docs or candidate JSON by hand.
chains.decision: Candidate decision evidence now exposes next_command for the chosen next_artifact, preserving the executable follow-up path through the decision layer.

chains.observation: CI could catch claim binding drift, but local commits still depended on humans remembering the verifier.
chains.hypothesis: A pre-commit hook can run loop registry claim/doc/impact verification before PR creation.
chains.decision: Local pre-commit now blocks claim binding drift before review.

chains.observation: Closed-loop tools used different verification flags, leaving agents to remember tool-specific commands.
chains.hypothesis: A shared -verify intent lets agents and pre-commit invoke closed-loop verification without reading each tool's prose usage.
chains.decision: Closed-loop verifier tools expose a common -verify intent so execution can be driven by policy instead of human command memory.

chains.observation: A staging runtime settings page can show a local daemon offline after the desktop app gracefully stops its desktop-managed daemon on app quit.
chains.hypothesis: Cross-repository daemon lifecycle ambiguity should be captured as an owned executable open question instead of staying in operator memory or being patched in the public control-plane runtime path.
chains.decision: Desktop daemon lifecycle/profile ownership remains an executable open decision until a desktop-owned manifest defines app quit, profile isolation, and stop-source evidence behavior.

chains.observation: Marketing, analysis, and intent-oriented task documents can be misread as executable instructions, while token or cloud-credit exhaustion can leak provider wording into the AI Agent thread.
chains.hypothesis: A prompt interaction policy plus visible-message normalization can keep the existing thread conversational: ambiguous task context asks for intent first, concrete follow-up instructions become authoritative, and provider limits render as a stable user-facing result without changing API shape.
chains.decision: Ambiguous task intent handling and provider-limit copy are enforced as an AI thread history claim while preserving existing endpoint input and output fields.

chains.observation: Claim-bound files can drift without running the loop-registry PR impact gate when workflow path filters omit newly bound code, tests, fixtures, manifests, or generated readers.
chains.hypothesis: The loop-registry verifier can read its own workflow path filters and fail when any claim-bound surface is not covered, so agents do not need to remember trigger maintenance manually.
chains.decision: Loop-registry workflow trigger coverage is now part of claim binding verification: every claim-bound path must be included directly or through a directory glob before a PR can pass.

chains.observation: Loop-registry business claims can exist without an evidence graph chain that explains the observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next loop behind that claim.
chains.hypothesis: Adding explicit claim references to evidence graph chains and verifying full claim coverage keeps claim meaning connected to executable reasoning instead of narrative memory.
chains.decision: Evidence graph verification now fails when any loop-registry claim lacks a chain or any chain references an unknown claim.

chains.observation: Evidence graph chains can reference code, workflows, tools, or manifests that do not trigger the evidence-graph workflow when they change.
chains.hypothesis: The evidence graph verifier can read its own workflow path filters and fail when any non-artifact chain reference is outside those filters, keeping graph evidence refreshed without asking agents to remember trigger maintenance.
chains.decision: Evidence graph workflow trigger coverage is part of graph verification: referenced non-artifact surfaces must be covered by direct paths or directory globs.

loop.observation: Evidence artifacts existed, but the reasoning chain from observation to next loop was still scattered across generated readers and PR memory.
loop.hypothesis: A compact evidence graph can make the development loop navigable by tools without asking an AI to read every narrative document.
loop.execute: Verify every chain has observation, hypothesis, change, verifier, evidence, decision, and next-loop nodes; verify repository refs exist; generate this reader and publish graph evidence in CI.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on incomplete chains, duplicate ids, missing refs, stale generated docs, missing strict workflow evidence, or missing redaction on artifact evidence.
loop.retrospective: This makes the evidence loop itself inspectable: future agents can see why a loop exists, what changed, what verifies it, and what loop should run next.
